protocol.repair_policy: A repair is a separately reviewed proposal. It never overwrites or silently weakens the pinned source theorem, and formalization artifacts may not be accepted as source corrections. Every reviewed repair is bound to its exact proposal payload and an independent repair-review packet.

source.anchor: Section 1.3, printed/PDF page 5, general Glauber update steps 2–3; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.13826v4#page=5. Two short formula/instruction excerpts below. ASTIS context paraphrase (not source quotation): the source uses a distribution on Omega subset of {0,1}^V, a finite site set V and a starting configuration X_t in Omega; step 2 applies to every w != v. The preceding uniform-site selection step is outside this fixed-site comparison.
source.original_text:
X_{t+1}(w) = X_t(v).
Choose X_{t+1}(v) from the conditional Gibbs distribution μ(σ(v) = · | σ(w) = X_t(w) for all w ≠ v).

lean.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (X : Fin (n + 1) → Type u_1) [inst : (j : Fin (n + 1)) → MeasurableSpace (X j)] (μ : Measure ((j : Fin (n + 1)) → X j)) [inst_1 : IsFiniteMeasure μ] (i : Fin (n + 1)) [inst_2 : StandardBorelSpace (X i)] [inst_3 : Nonempty (X i)] [MeasurableSingletonClass ((j : Fin n) → X (i.succAbove j))] (x : (j : Fin (n + 1)) → X j), μ {y | (fun j => y (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)} ≠ 0 → (CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath X μ i) x = μ[|{y | (fun j => y (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)}]
decoder_context: Fin (n+1) is the finite index type; i.succAbove : Fin n → Fin (n+1) enumerates the indices other than i in increasing order. The universe u_1 is arbitrary.
e_i is the measurable equivalence x ↦ ((fun j => x (i.succAbove j)), x i), with inverse reinserting the selected coordinate.

For ν = μ.map e_i, let κ = condDistrib Prod.snd Prod.fst ν. condDistrib Y Z ν is the selected regular conditional-distribution Markov kernel, defined as the conditional kernel of ν.map (fun a => (Z a, Y a)); it is characterized ν.map Z-almost everywhere.
CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath X μ i x = (e_i.symm)_# (dirac ((e_i x).1) × κ ((e_i x).1)); measure map denotes pushforward, and the product is the product of measures.

μ[|s] denotes ProbabilityTheory.cond μ s, defined as (μ s)⁻¹ • μ.restrict s. The scalar is ENNReal with totalized inverse. IsFiniteMeasure means finite total mass; no normalization to mass one is built into that class.

reconstruction.text: Let n be any natural number, let (X_j) indexed by Fin(n+1) be measurable spaces, and let μ be a finite measure on their dependent product Ω = ∏_j X_j. Fix i ∈ Fin(n+1). Assume X_i is a nonempty standard Borel space and the complementary product Ω_{-i} = ∏_{j∈Fin(n)} X_{i.succAbove(j)} has measurable singletons. Write r_i(x) = (x_{i.succAbove(j)})_j and e_i(x) = (r_i(x), x_i). Let κ be the selected regular conditional-distribution kernel of the second coordinate given the first under (e_i)_#μ, and define H_i(x) = (e_i^{-1})_#(δ_{r_i(x)} × κ(r_i(x))). Then, for every x ∈ Ω whose complementary-coordinate fiber F_x = {y ∈ Ω : r_i(y) = r_i(x)} has nonzero μ-measure, H_i(x) = (μ(F_x))^{-1} • (μ restricted to F_x). Thus the coordinate heat-bath measure at every such x equals μ conditioned on that fiber.

objects.original: A distribution μ on Ω ⊆ {0,1}^V, a current configuration X_t, a selected site v, and the next configuration X_{t+1}.
objects.reconstructed: A finite measure μ on a dependent product of measurable spaces, a selected coordinate i, a complementary-coordinate fiber F_x, and a coordinate heat-bath measure H_i(x) constructed using a conditional-distribution kernel.
objects.evidence: The source's conditional sampling instruction has a measure/kernel interpretation. The reconstruction explicitly supplies that interpretation. Its enlarged domains and changed joint-update conclusion require separate assessment below.

domains.original: The supplied context paraphrase specifies a finite site set V, Boolean configurations, Ω ⊆ {0,1}^V, a probability distribution on Ω, and X_t ∈ Ω.
domains.reconstructed: Coordinates are indexed by Fin(n+1), each coordinate has an arbitrary measurable space, μ is any finite measure on the full dependent product, and x is any product element satisfying the positive-fiber premise.
domains.evidence: The Lean statement quantifies over X : Fin(n+1) → Type, MeasurableSpace instances and IsFiniteMeasure μ. It does not impose Boolean coordinates, probability normalization, a distinguished subset Ω, or x ∈ Ω. A Boolean probability measure on Ω can be represented on the ambient cube, but that representation is an additional elaboration, not an identification stated in the excerpt.

quantifiers.original: For a current configuration X_t ∈ Ω and a selected site v, the supplied context says step 2 applies to every w ≠ v; step 3 samples the selected coordinate conditional on the old complementary coordinates.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every n, eligible measurable family X, finite measure μ, selected coordinate i and configuration x, the equality holds only if μ(F_x) ≠ 0.
quantifiers.evidence: The reconstructed assertion is universal over substantially more ambient spaces and measures, while its pointwise conclusion is restricted by an explicit nonzero-fiber implication. The excerpt/context does not state that restriction. The source's every-w complementary update also differs from the reconstructed update, as recorded under conclusion.

assumptions.original: The supplied context gives a finite Boolean configuration space and a probability distribution. The displayed conditional sampling instruction presupposes a meaningful conditional law, but neither excerpt nor context explicitly asserts μ(F_x) > 0 or defines Ω as the positive-probability support.
assumptions.reconstructed: μ is finite; X_i is nonempty and standard Borel; the complementary product has measurable singletons; and μ(F_x) ≠ 0.
assumptions.evidence: The positive-fiber premise appears explicitly in the Lean implication. Membership x ∈ Ω alone does not imply μ(F_x) > 0 under the supplied context. The measurable-space requirements are automatic for the usual finite discrete Boolean specialization, but matter in the generalized domain. Conversely, finite measure is a weaker normalization requirement than probability distribution.

conclusion.original: Taken literally, step 2 sets X_{t+1}(w) = X_t(v) for every w ≠ v. Step 3 draws X_{t+1}(v) conditional on σ(w) = X_t(w) for every w ≠ v.
conclusion.reconstructed: H_i(x) equals the normalized restriction of μ to F_x = {y : y_{-i} = x_{-i}}. Therefore the complementary coordinates retain their own old values almost surely, and the selected coordinate has the corresponding conditional law.
conclusion.evidence: Literal step 2 copies the old selected-coordinate value into each other coordinate. The reconstruction instead preserves each other coordinate's old value. For V = {0,1}, v = 0, x = (0,1), and uniform μ on the Boolean square, μ(F_x) = 1/2. The reconstruction gives the next second coordinate equal to 1 almost surely, whereas literal step 2 gives it equal to 0 almost surely. Both sides have a well-defined selected-coordinate conditional law in this example, so the discrepancy is not caused by zero conditioning mass.

scopes.original: A fixed-site, one-step comparison of general Glauber update steps 2–3. The packet expressly excludes the preceding uniform-site selection step.
scopes.reconstructed: A pointwise identity for the heat-bath measure at one fixed coordinate, subject to a positive-fiber premise.
scopes.evidence: Both supplied comparison targets concern a single selected coordinate. Neither the reconstructed proposition nor this review establishes the full random-site transition, an iterated trajectory, stationarity, mixing, or any global sampling guarantee.

constant_dependencies.original: No numerical estimate or auxiliary numerical constant appears. The conditional update depends on μ, the selected site v, and the current complementary configuration.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: No numerical estimate or auxiliary numerical constant appears. H_i(x) and the conditioning fiber depend on X, μ, i and x; the normalization is μ(F_x)^{-1}.
constant_dependencies.evidence: There are no bound constants to compare. The reconstruction's reciprocal fiber mass is the ordinary conditional-measure normalization, not an additional free constant.

deltas.description: The literal nonselected-coordinate assignment disagrees with the fiber-conditioned joint law. The discrepancy may be a source or excerpt error, but cannot be silently corrected or treated as exact fidelity.
deltas.evidence: Pinned original_text says X_{t+1}(w) = X_t(v). The reconstruction conditions the next full configuration on y_{-i} = x_{-i}. With uniform μ on {0,1}^2, selected coordinate 0 and x = (0,1), the two next-step distributions have disjoint supports according to the second coordinate.

deltas.description: The theorem explicitly excludes zero-mass complementary fibers. The provided source evidence does not establish that all starting configurations have positive-mass fibers.
deltas.evidence: The Lean statement requires μ {y | r_i(y) = r_i(x)} ≠ 0. The source context supplies only X_t ∈ Ω. For example, Ω may be the entire Boolean square while μ is concentrated at (0,0); the point (0,1) belongs to Ω but its complementary fiber for site 0 has zero mass.

deltas.description: The reconstructed theorem generalizes from a finite Boolean probability model on a subset to arbitrary eligible measurable coordinate spaces and finite measures on the full product.
deltas.evidence: The packet contrasts Ω ⊆ {0,1}^V and a distribution with arbitrary X, MeasurableSpace instances and IsFiniteMeasure μ. A finite Boolean specialization is available mathematically, but the supplied excerpt does not itself claim the generalized theorem.

deltas.description: The universal reconstructed assertion ranges over broader objects but covers only configurations with positive-mass complementary fibers. This is not an unqualified translation of the supplied update instruction.
deltas.evidence: The theorem's final premise is a nonzero-fiber implication for every ambient x. The source/context supplies an update at X_t ∈ Ω without stating the corresponding support restriction or a convention for null conditioning events.

source_review.evidence:
This review used only the designated anti-anchored packet. I did not inspect repository instructions, implementation bodies, prior reviews, repair suggestions, other agents' work, or external sources. Independence here means that the reviewer is distinct from the stated formalizer and blind decoder and assessed the supplied source evidence against their supplied artifacts independently.

The decisive finding is a direct mathematical counterexample on the finite Boolean domain itself. Let V = {0,1}, select v = 0, take x = (0,1), and let μ assign mass 1/4 to every configuration. Conditioning on the old complementary coordinate gives F_x = {(0,1),(1,1)} of mass 1/2. The reconstructed law is uniform on this fiber. The literal source instructions instead set the next second coordinate to x_0 = 0 and sample the first coordinate uniformly, yielding a law on {(0,0),(1,0)}. Thus the two laws differ even when every reconstructed assumption is satisfied. The selected-coordinate conditional marginal is compatible in this example; the nonselected-coordinate assignment is not.

The instruction pair suggests a possible indexing error in the pinned step 2, because step 3 conditions on old complementary values whereas step 2 overwrites those values with the old selected value. Nevertheless, the available evidence does not establish whether the published PDF contains that error, whether the packet excerpt is inaccurate, or whether omitted context changes its interpretation. Consequently, possible-source-error is a diagnosis of the supplied source representation, not a verified erratum to the publication.

Independently, positive complementary-fiber mass is a genuine qualification. It would follow from μ({x}) > 0 in the finite model, but the packet does not state that Ω is precisely positive-probability support or that the current state has positive mass. The source's conditional-law instruction therefore remains underspecified at null conditioning events relative to the explicit theorem premise. I cannot classify this premise as merely an exposed source-implicit assumption on the evidence provided.

The generalized measure-theoretic setting can contain the usual finite Boolean specialization, with the source measure embedded in an ambient product and the relevant measurability assumptions supplied. This gives a plausible relationship between the mathematical constructions but does not erase the literal assignment discrepancy, prove the source's unstated support assumptions, or make the generalization an exact source statement.

The packet reports that the Lean statement compiled. I have not independently checked compilation, the proof, or the definition of CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath. Its conditional-kernel interpretation is supplied by the blind reconstruction and is not recoverable in full from the opaque declaration name alone. Accordingly, conclusions about that implementation are conditional on the supplied reconstruction accurately describing it.

The source evidence consists of two short excerpts plus an explicitly nonquoted context paraphrase. This limits conclusions about the surrounding publication and prevents verification of source transcription or broader conventions. The reviewer_packet_sha256 value is copied from the packet's provided packet_sha256 field; I did not produce or independently verify a packet hash. review_run_sha256 is intentionally empty for the root to populate by hashing the immutable returned record. No repair is approved.
source_review.interpretation: Accepted means acceptance of this documented discrepancy diagnosis. It does not mean acceptance of the formalization as an exact rendering of the pinned source, acceptance of a corrected source, or approval of any repair.

review.evidence: Independent exact-proposal review of ASTIS-REPAIR-20260908-GlauberCopyIndex only. I inspected the generated packet and the cited primary PDF, not prior verdicts, registries, worker files, histories, other repair proposals, or implementation files. My reviewer identity differs from positive_fiber_worker and math_decoder. I independently obtained PDF SHA256 3cc2f911b33bb5538157ef8a70f0c7e0f3c812ecd06dc9c1d5ea0bfdae11a52a and visually inspected both complete printed/PDF pages 4 and 5, newly rendered from that verified file. Page 4, section 1.1 (Setting), defines Omega as precisely the Boolean configurations with strictly positive probability. Page 5, section 1.3 (Glauber dynamics/Gibbs sampler), prints the disputed assignment with right-hand-side index v, but the immediately following explanation requires retaining every unselected spin and resampling only the selected spin. Step 3 also explicitly conditions on each complementary coordinate's own old value. These independent textual constraints support replacing only the step-2 right-hand-side v with w. This is a one-index micro-correction of the literal formula, justified by the source's own explanation, not merely by compatibility with the proposed Lean proof. Uniform site selection and the selected-coordinate conditional law remain unchanged. No new positivity premise is needed in the source's finite Boolean setting: for x in Omega and F_x = {y : y(w) = x(w) for every w != v}, the inclusion {x} subset F_x gives mu(F_x) >= mu({x}) > 0. The proposed mathematical witness is valid: for the two-site point mass at x = (0,1), selecting site 0 copies the old 0 into coordinate 1, while conditioning on the old coordinate-1 value 1 forces the new coordinate 0 to be 0, yielding (0,0). Selecting site 1 similarly yields (1,1). Both conditioning events have probability one, both literal outputs lie outside Omega = {(0,1)}, and the corrected assignment leaves x fixed for either site. This calculation is an independent mathematical check, not a Lean-certified counterexample. Acceptance is restricted to this exact source-implicit index correction and its stated source-setting reconstruction. It does not certify all differences between the finite Boolean source and the packet's more general finite-measure/dependent-product Lean statement, validate the implementation or regular conditional-kernel construction, supply a complete source-to-Lean fidelity verdict, or certify a random-site algorithm, sweep, reversibility, or mixing result. The packet and proposal canonical SHA256 values were independently recomputed by sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON serialization after excluding their respective hash fields and match the values below; the packet file's separate raw-byte SHA256 is 1ad678c1d221062b1afafbc6b2b34475a6301b8a7e2648c7d5dd1e256eb7319e. No self-referential review-run hash is asserted; the coordinating reviewer may hash this immutable result externally.

This is the fixed-site substep of the source's uniform random-site update; no sweep, reversibility, or mixing conclusion is added.
repairs.justification: The complete pinned PDF page 5 has adjacent prose describing retention of the complementary coordinates. Page 4 section 1.1 defines Omega by strictly positive configuration probability, so a source-valid initial configuration has positive mass and every retained-coordinate fiber containing it has positive mass. The printed step-2 index instead copies the selected site's old value into other sites and can leave Omega even when all relevant conditional events have mass one. The correction addresses that index only, not a Lean typeclass or totalized-conditional convenience.
repairs.minimality_evidence: Exactly one right-hand-side index changes in step 2. The source distribution, positive-support state set, uniform site selection and step-3 conditional law are unchanged. No new regularity, positivity, normalization, clock, temperature, irreducibility, reversibility or complexity premise is inserted. The original text and its hash remain immutable evidence.
repairs.reference_or_counterexample: Chen–Štefankovič–Vigoda arXiv:2307.13826v4, section 1.1 printed/PDF p.4 and section 1.3 printed/PDF p.5; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.13826v4#page=4 and #page=5; PDF SHA256 3cc2f911b33bb5538157ef8a70f0c7e0f3c812ecd06dc9c1d5ea0bfdae11a52a. Mathematical witness, not a Lean-certified counterexample: on two Boolean coordinates let mu be the point mass at (0,1), so Omega={(0,1)}. source.anchor: Section 1.1, unnumbered support definition, printed/PDF p.4; section 1.3 general update step 1 (site selection), step 3 (conditional sampling), and the explanatory prose immediately after step 3, printed/PDF p.5. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.13826v4#page=4 and #page=5. This comparison targets that explanatory update rule and its one-step law.
source.original_text: ASTIS mathematical paraphrase, not source quotation: Let V be a finite nonempty set of sites and let μ be a probability distribution on the Boolean configurations. Its state space Ω consists of exactly the configurations of positive probability. Starting at x in Ω, select one site i uniformly from V. Retain each other site's own old value and sample the value at i from the target conditional on all the retained values. Identify the probability of each configuration y after this one update. Coordinates are represented by Fin(n+1) and Boolean values by Bool; this is a coordinate convention, not a sweep or a convergence claim.
source.wording_status: faithful ASTIS paraphrase of the cited explanatory route; not licensed source text

lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (μ : Measure (Fin (n + 1) → Bool)) [inst : IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (x y : Fin (n + 1) → Bool),
  μ {x} ≠ 0 →
    ((randomScan μ) x) {y} =
      (↑n + 1)⁻¹ *
        ∑ i,
          if ∀ (j : Fin (n + 1)), j ≠ i → y j = x j then
            (μ {z | (fun j => z (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)})⁻¹ * μ {y}
          else 0
decoder_context: Bool={false,true} has its standard discrete measurable structure; function spaces carry the product measurable structure. Measure and IsProbabilityMeasure denote a measure and total mass one. μ{x} is singleton mass in extended nonnegative reals.

For i:Fin(n+1), i.succAbove:Fin n→Fin(n+1) is the increasing bijection onto all indices except i. Define r_i(z)=(fun j=>z(i.succAbove j)) and e_i(z)=(r_i(z),z i); e_i is the corresponding measurable equivalence.

Write ν_i=(e_i)_#μ. Let C_i be the regular conditional distribution of the second component given the first under ν_i, selected as a Markov kernel by the ambient library. Set H_i(x)=(e_i⁻¹)_#(δ_{r_i(x)}⊗C_i(r_i(x))). Here # denotes pushforward and δ a Dirac measure.

randomScan μ is the finite sum over i:Fin(n+1) of H_i.withDensity(fun _ _ => (↑((n+1:ℝ≥0)⁻¹):ℝ≥0∞)); withDensity multiplies the component kernel's output measure by the stated constant density. The weights are state-independent.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n, every probability measure μ on Ω = {false,true}^{Fin(n+1)}, and every x,y ∈ Ω, if μ({x}) > 0, then the singleton transition mass of the defined random-scan kernel is Pμ(x,{y}) = (n+1)⁻¹ ∑_{i∈Fin(n+1)} [if y_j = x_j for every j ≠ i, then μ({z∈Ω : r_i(z)=r_i(x)})⁻¹ μ({y}), else 0], where r_i deletes coordinate i. The kernel Pμ is the uniform mixture of the coordinate-update kernels constructed using the library-selected regular conditional distributions. Arithmetic in the displayed Lean equality takes place in the extended nonnegative reals.

objects.original: Section 1.1 introduces a distribution μ on a subset of binary configurations {0,1}^V and defines Ω to be exactly its positive-probability support. The selected Section 1.3 target chooses one vertex uniformly and resamples its spin from μ conditional on the fixed spins at the other vertices. The graph supplies the vertex set but its edges do not occur in this general conditional-update rule.
objects.reconstructed: A probability measure μ on the full finite Boolean cube Fin(n+1) → Bool, a current configuration x, an output configuration y, and the randomScan kernel. The blind reconstruction describes randomScan as the uniform mixture of coordinate-update kernels obtained from regular conditional distributions.
objects.evidence: Full visual inspection of printed/PDF p.4, Section 1.1, and p.5, Section 1.3, shows that Bool represents the two source spin values. A distribution on the source support can be extended by zero to the ambient cube, and any probability measure on the finite cube has exactly such a positive support. No graph-edge dependence is needed for this particular one-update law. The description of the implementation using regular conditional distributions comes from the blind reconstruction, not from independent inspection of Lean definitions.

domains.original: A finite vertex set V of cardinality N, a support Ω = {σ ∈ {0,1}^V : μ(σ) > 0}, and an input X_t ∈ Ω. Uniform selection of a vertex presupposes N > 0. The source update takes values in Ω.
domains.reconstructed: The site type is Fin(n+1), so every represented site set has positive size. x and y are quantified over the ambient cube, while μ{x} ≠ 0 restricts the asserted law to supported inputs. The formula also states zero transition mass at every unsupported output y. The decoder's symbol Ω denotes the full cube, unlike the source's Ω, which denotes positive support.
domains.evidence: The support equality is printed on p.4; the general update on p.5 begins from X_t ∈ Ω. Relabelling any finite nonempty V through a bijection with Fin(N), with N=n+1, gives the Lean indexing. The input condition is not a full-support hypothesis on μ. If μ{y}=0, every matching-site term is zero and every nonmatching term is explicitly zero, giving the harmless ambient-output extension. Although the reconstructed kernel exists on ambient null inputs, this theorem makes no claim about its law there. The decoder's reuse of Ω must not be mistaken for a change to the source support definition.

quantifiers.original: The general distribution update applies to any binary distribution in the Section 1.1 setting and any supported current state; its one-step transition law determines probabilities of possible output configurations. A site is chosen uniformly from the whole vertex set.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every natural n, every probability measure μ on Fin(n+1) → Bool, and every ambient x and y, the stated equality holds whenever μ{x} ≠ 0. The displayed finite sum ranges over every i ∈ Fin(n+1), and agreement with x is required at every j distinct from i.
quantifiers.evidence: The Section 1.3 paragraph introducing the general definition on p.5 is not limited to the preceding hard-core example. The Lean quantifiers cover every positive finite cardinality by writing N=n+1. They provide the pointwise law at every supported input, not merely an almost-everywhere assertion. Quantifying y over the ambient cube is the zero-extension of the support-indexed transition law, not an assertion that null configurations are supported.

assumptions.original: μ is a probability distribution; the system is binary and finite; the current state has positive probability by membership in Ω. Selecting a vertex uniformly requires a nonempty vertex set. The specifically cited general conditional-update rule requires no hard-core activity, graph connectivity, full support, or irreducibility assumption.
assumptions.reconstructed: IsProbabilityMeasure μ, the finite nonempty site type Fin(n+1), Boolean spins, and the hypothesis μ{x} ≠ 0. No other mathematical hypotheses appear in the supplied Lean statement.
assumptions.evidence: For a nonnegative measure, μ{x} ≠ 0 is exactly μ{x} > 0. For each selected i, the conditioning fibre E_i = {z : z agrees with x off i} contains x, so 0 < μ{x} ≤ μ(E_i) ≤ 1. Thus the conditional denominator is positive and finite at all inputs covered by the theorem. Fin(n+1) exposes the nonemptiness presupposed by p.5's uniform vertex choice rather than requiring an extra positive-support condition at every configuration. The surrounding hard-core discussion is not an assumption of the later general update.

conclusion.original: For the cited explanatory rule, all unselected spins retain their own previous values and the selected spin is sampled conditionally on those retained values. This determines the probability of each configuration after one uniformly selected coordinate update; the source does not print the displayed finite-sum singleton formula.
conclusion.reconstructed: The singleton transition mass is (n+1)⁻¹ times the sum over sites i of μ(E_i)⁻¹ μ{y} when y agrees with x away from i, and zero otherwise, with E_i expressed by deleting coordinate i using i.succAbove. The equality is in the extended nonnegative reals.
conclusion.evidence: For fixed i, a nonmatching y is impossible under retained off-site values. For matching y, the event specifying the retained values together with the newly sampled value y_i is exactly {y}, so its conditional probability is μ{y}/μ(E_i). Averaging over the uniform site choice gives exactly the displayed equality. The map i.succAbove enumerates all sites other than i, so the conditioning event represents all and only the retained coordinates. Positivity and finiteness of μ(E_i) make the extended-nonnegative-real arithmetic coincide with the ordinary finite conditional-probability ratio. Diagonal transitions are included: when y=x, all selected sites contribute their respective holding probability. This is a semantic derivation from the supplied statement and source context, not verification of the Lean proof or kernel implementation.

scopes.original: The pinned comparison explicitly selects Section 1.1's support definition and Section 1.3's general site-selection step, conditional-sampling step, and explanatory prose immediately after that sampling step. It concerns one transition X_t → X_{t+1}.
scopes.reconstructed: The theorem identifies the one-step singleton law of the uniform random-scan kernel at supported inputs. It does not concern a sweep, several updates, convergence, stationarity, mixing time, or the full range of claims in the monograph.
scopes.evidence: On the fully inspected p.5, the explanatory prose says to fix all vertices except the selected one, and the conditional expression conditions on σ(w)=X_t(w) for all w distinct from that vertex. However, the adjacent general numbered step 2 literally writes X_{t+1}(w)=X_t(v), using the selected vertex's old value instead of w's own old value. That line conflicts with the specifically cited explanatory target and is excluded by the packet's stated scope. Acceptance here therefore does not certify the literal full numbered algorithm. It also does not certify the preceding hard-core ergodicity discussion or the subsequent mixing-time definition.

constant_dependencies.original: The site-selection probability is exactly 1/|V| per vertex. Conditional probabilities depend on μ and the off-site values of the current state, through the mass of the corresponding conditioning fibre. There is one selected-site update per time step.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The exact prefactor is (↑n+1)⁻¹, the inverse of the cardinality of Fin(n+1). Each matching term has exactly one inverse fibre mass multiplied by μ{y}; the sum has n+1 terms. There is no activity parameter, extra lazy factor, sweep normalization, or unspecified asymptotic constant.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The source's n=|V| and the Lean parameter n differ by the explicit cardinality convention N=n+1; the physical number of sites, and hence the update rate, agree. For N=1 the deleted-coordinate fibre is the full cube, its mass is 1, and the formula reduces to μ{y}, as a one-site resampling must. For general N the selected site is uniform on all sites, not only feasible or changing sites. The displayed normalizer depends only on μ, i, and x off i, and the output numerator is precisely μ{y}; there is no hidden dependence on edges or the preceding hard-core parameter λ.

source.anchor: Levin–Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition, Section 3.3.2, printed pp.42–43 / PDF pp.58–59, equations (3.6)–(3.7), and Exercise 3.2, printed p.45 / PDF p.61. Boolean specialization of the reversibility clause only; https://pages.uoregon.edu/dlevin/MARKOV/mcmt2e.pdf#page=58 .
source.original_text: ASTIS faithful mathematical paraphrase of the Boolean specialization, not a quotation: Let V be a finite nonempty set of sites, let μ be a probability distribution on Boolean configurations, and let Ω be its positive-probability support. In one update from x in Ω, select a site uniformly, retain the other sites at their own old values, and draw the selected site's value from μ conditional on those retained values. This Glauber chain is reversible for μ: target-weighted transition flow from any subset A of Ω to any subset B equals the reverse flow. The finite site labels can be represented by Fin(n+1). This target records the reversibility clause, not the source's arbitrary finite-spin-alphabet generality, its separate stationary-law consequence, or any convergence claim.
source.wording_status: faithful ASTIS paraphrase of explicitly selected Boolean reversibility clause; not original source text

decoder_context: Fin(n+1) has n+1 sites and Bool has two values, with the product of discrete measurable structures. μ is a measure on this finite configuration space; IsProbabilityMeasure μ means μ(univ)=1.

For i:Fin(n+1), let r_i(x) be the retained tuple (x(i.succAbove j)) indexed by j:Fin n. Let e_i(x)=(r_i(x),x i); this is the measurable coordinate-splitting equivalence. Its inverse inserts the selected value into the retained tuple.

Write ν_i=(e_i)_#μ, with # meaning pushforward. Let C_i be the library-selected regular conditional Markov distribution of the second component given the first under ν_i. Define H_i(x)=(e_i⁻¹)_#(δ_{r_i(x)}⊗C_i(r_i(x))). Here δ is a Dirac probability and ⊗ is the product measure. The conditional-distribution characterization is only first-marginal-almost-everywhere; no normalized-fiber value is stipulated at null retained inputs.

The kernel named randomScan μ in the statement is the finite sum of H_i with the constant, state-independent weight 1/(n+1) for every i. The construction uses the corresponding NNReal constant densities on component kernels.

Kernel.IsReversible K μ is defined as follows: for every pair of measurable sets A and B, the nonnegative set integral of x↦K(x,B) over A under μ equals the nonnegative set integral of y↦K(y,A) over B under μ. Both integrals take values in the extended nonnegative reals.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n and every probability measure μ on the finite binary configuration space X = {x : Fin(n+1) → Bool}, equipped with the product discrete measurable structure, the following uniformly weighted random-scan kernel K is reversible with respect to μ. For each site i, let r_i(x) retain all coordinates other than i, let e_i(x) = (r_i(x), x(i)) be the coordinate-splitting measurable equivalence, and let C_i be the library-selected regular conditional Markov distribution of the second coordinate given the first under the pushforward (e_i)_#μ. Define H_i(x) = (e_i⁻¹)_#(δ_{r_i(x)} ⊗ C_i(r_i(x))) and K(x) = Σ_{i∈Fin(n+1)} [1/(n+1)] H_i(x). The conditional-distribution characterization of C_i holds only almost everywhere with respect to the retained-coordinate marginal; no particular normalized-fiber value is specified at null retained inputs. Then for every pair of measurable sets A,B ⊆ X, the extended-nonnegative set integrals satisfy ∫⁻_{x∈A} K(x,B) dμ(x) = ∫⁻_{y∈B} K(y,A) dμ(y).

objects.original: Section 3.3.2 defines a single-site Glauber chain: choose a site uniformly, preserve all other coordinates, and sample from the target distribution conditioned on that retained configuration. The selected target specializes the finite spin alphabet to Bool.
objects.reconstructed: The kernel splits off one Boolean coordinate, preserves the retained coordinates through a Dirac measure, resamples the selected coordinate using a library-selected conditional Markov distribution, reconstructs the configuration, and averages these kernels uniformly.
objects.evidence: PDF p.58 / printed p.42, equation (3.6), fixes every coordinate other than the selected site; PDF p.59 / printed p.43, equation (3.7), gives the normalized conditional distribution. The packet's blind_reconstruction describes the same retain/resample/reassemble operation. On every positive-mass retained configuration, finite-space conditional distributions satisfy that normalized formula pointwise.

domains.original: The source chain has state space equal to the positive-probability support of a distribution on S^V. Within the selected Boolean specialization, this is Ω ⊆ Bool^V.
domains.reconstructed: The kernel is defined on the entire finite discrete cube X = Fin(n+1) → Bool, with an arbitrary probability measure μ that need not give positive mass to every configuration.
domains.evidence: PDF p.58 / printed p.42 explicitly makes the source state space the support and restricts equation (3.6) to states in that support. The packet reconstruction instead uses the ambient cube. If μ({x}) > 0, every retained-coordinate fiber through x has positive mass; equation (3.7) then identifies the reconstructed update and shows it remains in Ω. Consequently its restriction to Ω is the source chain, while μ-weighted transition integrals ignore ambient starting states outside Ω.

quantifiers.original: For every finite nonempty site set and every Boolean-configuration probability distribution, the resulting Glauber chain is reversible. The selected paraphrase expresses reversibility for every pair of subsets of its support.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every natural n and every probability measure μ on Fin(n+1) → Bool, the selected random-scan kernel satisfies the equality for every pair of measurable subsets of the ambient cube.
quantifiers.evidence: The source's general construction on PDF pp.58–59 ranges over finite site sets and probability distributions. Every finite nonempty site set admits a relabeling by Fin(n+1). Every subset of a finite discrete cube is measurable. The ambient-set equality reduces to the equality for intersections with Ω, because the measure is concentrated on Ω and updates starting in Ω stay there.

assumptions.original: Finite site and spin sets, a probability distribution, and use of its support as the chain's state space. Nonemptiness of the site set is implicit in selecting a site uniformly. Positive support ensures that each conditioning denominator used from a chain state is positive.
assumptions.reconstructed: Finite nonempty sites and Boolean spins are encoded in the type; μ is assumed to be a probability measure. No full-support assumption on the ambient cube is imposed. Conditional characterization is only almost everywhere under each retained-coordinate marginal.
assumptions.evidence: PDF p.58 states finiteness and the support condition and prescribes uniform site selection. Equations (3.6)–(3.7) imply π(X(x,v)) ≥ π(x) > 0 for a source state x. In the finite reconstruction, almost-everywhere conditional characterization therefore determines the conditional law at every retained input arising from positive-support states. No irreducibility, graph structure, independence, or ambient strict-positivity assumption is needed for the selected clause.

conclusion.original: The selected clause states reversibility with respect to the target distribution for the support-state Glauber chain.
conclusion.reconstructed: For every measurable A,B in the ambient cube, the extended-nonnegative integrals of K(x,B) over A and K(y,A) over B against μ are equal.
conclusion.evidence: PDF p.59 / printed p.43 states reversibility, and Exercise 3.2 on PDF p.61 / printed p.45 asks for its verification. Independently, equations (3.6)–(3.7) give the symmetric single-site weighted flow π(x)π(y)/π(X(x,v)) when x and y agree off v, and zero otherwise. Uniform averaging preserves symmetry. Finite summation gives the set-integral equality, and singleton sets recover detailed balance. Both flow integrals are bounded by one.

scopes.original: The inspected source covers arbitrary finite spin alphabets and states both stationarity and reversibility. The packet explicitly pins only the Boolean specialization of the reversibility clause.
scopes.reconstructed: One-step Boolean random-scan reversibility, expressed for a selected conditional-kernel construction. The displayed declaration does not separately assert stationarity, convergence, mixing, or general finite-alphabet coverage.
scopes.evidence: PDF p.58 introduces arbitrary finite S; PDF p.59 and Exercise 3.2 state both stationarity and reversibility. The packet source.anchor and source.original_text explicitly exclude arbitrary-spin-alphabet generality and the separate stationary-law consequence. The supplied declaration and reconstruction match that selected scope, not the complete breadth of the source statement.

constant_dependencies.original: Each discrete update selects exactly one site uniformly, with weight 1/|V|, and uses a conditional law determined by the target distribution and retained coordinates.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: There are n+1 sites, each receiving mixture weight 1/(n+1). Conditional kernels depend on μ and the selected site; the scan weight does not depend on μ or the current configuration.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Uniform site selection is prescribed on PDF pp.58–59. The packet reconstruction explicitly gives K as the sum of n+1 single-site kernels with coefficient 1/(n+1). Thus one kernel application corresponds to one source update, not an entire sweep or a rescaled continuous-time clock. No additional rate or quantitative bound occurs in the selected conclusion.

deltas.description: The formal target is a Boolean specialization, not a formalization of the source's arbitrary finite-spin-alphabet generality. This restriction is already explicit in the pinned target and is acceptable within that scope.
deltas.evidence: PDF p.58 / printed p.42, Section 3.3.2, allows an arbitrary finite set S. The packet source.anchor identifies a Boolean specialization; lean.statement and blind_reconstruction use Bool.

deltas.description: The source chain lives on positive support, whereas the reconstructed kernel lives on the full Boolean cube. These are not literally identical state-space presentations. Restriction to positive support identifies the source chain, and the ambient extension leaves the selected μ-weighted reversibility statement unchanged.
deltas.evidence: PDF p.58 explicitly sets the source state space equal to the support. Equations (3.6)–(3.7) restrict its updates to support configurations. The packet reconstruction admits arbitrary μ on the full cube. For positive-support x, the retained fiber has mass at least μ({x}) > 0, so the reconstructed conditional update assigns zero mass outside support; ambient source states outside support have zero μ-weight.

deltas.description: The reconstruction uses a selected regular conditional version, whose values at null retained inputs are not specified by normalized fibers. The source never needs those values. This does not permit a claim of pointwise equality with a source transition rule at every ambient null state. Null current states with positive-mass retained contexts still have their corresponding single-site conditional laws determined.
deltas.evidence: Equation (3.7) on PDF p.59 defines a normalized fiber law only for source states introduced in equation (3.6), whose fibers have positive mass. The packet blind_reconstruction explicitly limits its conditional characterization to almost everywhere under the retained marginal. On finite positive-mass retained atoms this determines the law exactly; a null retained fiber contains no positive-support starting state and therefore contributes no μ-weighted starting flow.

deltas.description: Nonempty sites are made explicit through Fin(n+1). The source's prose says finite sites without separately spelling out nonemptiness, but its instruction to choose a site uniformly presupposes it. No empty-site interpretation is certified here.
deltas.evidence: PDF p.58 / printed p.42 first introduces finite V and then instructs the chain to select a vertex uniformly from V. The packet's pinned paraphrase explicitly says nonempty, and lean.statement uses Fin(n+1), whose cardinality is always positive.

deltas.description: Finite-state reversibility is elaborated into an equality of extended-nonnegative set integrals over arbitrary ambient measurable sets. This is equivalent for the selected target, rather than an additional convergence or trajectory-level conclusion.
deltas.evidence: PDF p.59 and Exercise 3.2 assert reversibility. Equations (3.6)–(3.7) produce symmetric target-weighted single-site transition probabilities; summing over sites and then over pairs of states yields the reconstructed integral equality. Conversely, singleton sets recover the pairwise equality. Finite discrete measurability and the support reduction described in D2 justify the ambient-set formulation.
